inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL string-function example applies SOUNDEX to names to produce four-character phonetic keys.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored alias-review audit. Candidate and reference names exercise matching phonetic keys, different keys, and SQL NULL propagation; CASE classifies the comparison while the table, names, and reporting context are new.

fixture_notes: Alias 1201 compares Smith with Smythe, 1202 compares Robert with Rupert, and 1203 compares Ashcraft with Ashcroft; all three pairs share MariaDB phonetic keys. Alias 1204 has a NULL reference, and alias 1205 has a NULL candidate, so the classification must preserve the missing state instead of reporting a phonetic match.
determinism_notes: Alias IDs and names are fixed and ordered by the primary key; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE alias_reviews (review_id INT PRIMARY KEY, candidate_name VARCHAR(40) NULL, reference_name VARCHAR(40) NULL)
INSERT INTO alias_reviews VALUES (1201, 'Smith', 'Smythe'), (1202, 'Robert', 'Rupert'), (1203, 'Ashcraft', 'Ashcroft'), (1204, 'Green', NULL), (1205, NULL, 'Greene')

steps.sql: SELECT review_id, candidate_name, reference_name, SOUNDEX(candidate_name) AS candidate_key, SOUNDEX(reference_name) AS reference_key, CASE WHEN candidate_name IS NULL OR reference_name IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN SOUNDEX(candidate_name) = SOUNDEX(reference_name) THEN 'phonetic-match' ELSE 'different' END AS review_state FROM alias_reviews ORDER BY review_id
